summary: Pick out the incorrect statements about stock-in-trade costing: the methods available to cash-basis versus accrual-basis traders and how items that cannot be separately identified must be accounted for.
difficulty_basis: Single-concept recall with three closely worded statements; requires knowing which costing method each basis of accounting must use.

summary: Compute the taxable amount, if any, from a lump-sum insurance receipt for two stolen antique sculptures, weighing the payout against each item's acquisition cost and market value at theft.
difficulty_basis: Two-mark item needing per-asset gain/loss working and the rule on which personal assets escape the capital-gains charge.

summary: Identify which heads of income — property, other sources, capital gains, speculation gains — cannot be set against a loss from non-speculation business.
difficulty_basis: Direct recall of the loss set-off restrictions across heads; one step of reasoning.

summary: Name the pillar of tax administration most damaged when the authority selects a taxpayer for audit on secret risk parameters and refuses to explain the basis.
difficulty_basis: Straightforward recall of the four pillars; the scenario points plainly at one of them.

summary: Choose the deductible amount when a flour miller feeds wheat grown on his own land into his milling business: cultivation cost, market value at the time of use, both combined, or nothing because farm produce is exempt.
difficulty_basis: Single rule on agricultural produce diverted to business use; must resist the exemption distractor.

summary: For a non-resident Pakistani citizen earning local income under the normal regime plus foreign income, select which statements — return of income, wealth statement, foreign income and assets statement — he must file.
difficulty_basis: Filing-obligation recall for a non-resident citizen; two plausible distractors.

summary: For a cottage industry selling digitally ordered goods cash-on-delivery while the courier withholds 2% sales tax, pick the correct statement on registration duty and whether the withheld tax settles, prepays, or is adjustable against the liability.
difficulty_basis: Layered sales-tax concepts (cottage industry, e-marketplace withholding, registration) in one item.

summary: Where a supplier pockets sales tax instead of depositing it, decide when the buyer becomes jointly and severally liable — only with knowledge or reasonable suspicion of non-payment — and who must prove that knowledge.
difficulty_basis: Fine legal distinction on joint liability and burden of proof; options differ on a single condition.

summary: Compute total income, taxable income and tax for a production director who resigned after 11 months: salary and allowances, furnished flat valued at the higher of market rent and 45% of basic, maintenance reimbursement added back, provident-fund contributions with the exemption cap, share-scheme gain taxed as salary at transferability, waived notice-period salary, taxable PF interest, exempt PF payout, and a pension-scheme tax credit kept out of the capital-gains block.
difficulty_basis: Ten-mark salary computation with nine distinct adjustments; the PF interest, share scheme and tax-credit steps are classic error points.

summary: State the statutory due dates for eight filings: company returns for January–June and July–December year-ends, individual/AOP returns, discontinuance notice, return on discontinuance, return on the Commissioner's notice, revised return without prior approval, and revised wealth statement.
difficulty_basis: Pure recall of eight deadlines; marks come from completeness, not reasoning.

summary: Test two amended assessments for TY2019 against the limitation rules: the filed return as a deemed assessment with a five-year window, and the one-year window for a further amendment after an earlier one.
difficulty_basis: Date arithmetic plus the deemed-assessment concept; two limitation dates to pin down.

summary: Advise the company on remedies against the further amended assessment and the recovery notice: appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) or direct to the Tribunal, and applying for stay of the demand with its time limits.
difficulty_basis: Two remedy tracks with conditions; needs the stay-period mechanics, not just names.

summary: For office premises that left business use mid-year and were leased to a friend, work out the disposal gain — treating fair market value as cost where it exceeds cost — and the resulting property income with the repair allowance.
difficulty_basis: Two linked computations; the disposal-on-cessation and FMV-as-cost rules are the traps.

summary: Compute the gain or loss on disposal of plant by a company whose income was exempt until TY2025, arriving at written-down value after deducting depreciation and initial allowance for the exempt period.
difficulty_basis: Single disposal working; the exempt-period depreciation step is the key insight.

summary: Handle a delivery vehicle bought partly with a cash cheque where its value tops Rs 1 million: deny depreciation, restrict the cost base for the gain computation, then compute the disposal result.
difficulty_basis: Two linked rules (cash-payment restriction and cost restriction) before a simple gain working.

summary: From Gohar's study-abroad and travel history, determine his residential status using all the prescribed criteria — not just day count — and explain how his US interest income later remitted to Pakistan is taxed, including the returning-expatriate treatment.
difficulty_basis: Status determination plus foreign-income treatment; the 122-day trap is the classic error.

summary: Briefly define tax evasion and tax avoidance, drawing the line between unlawful concealment and lawful arrangement of affairs.
difficulty_basis: Straight definition recall at T1 level.

summary: Classify four scenarios as evasion or avoidance with reasons: donations to approved charities, a factory in an export processing zone, undeclared foreign income, and deliberately deferred sales recording.
difficulty_basis: Apply the evasion/avoidance distinction; each case needs a stated reason.

summary: Compare the sales-tax consequences for a registered person making taxable supplies to a registered buyer versus an unregistered buyer, covering further tax and the other distinguishing points.
difficulty_basis: Comparison of two buyer categories; further tax is the headline but not the whole answer.

summary: Compute the AOP's taxable income and tax: disallow the technical fee paid to a member, exclude the jointly owned rental income from the AOP, and apply minimum tax on turnover.
difficulty_basis: Short AOP computation with member-payment and minimum-tax adjustments.

summary: Compute each member's taxable income and tax: take the AOP share correctly (ignoring the loss share), add each member's own income — trading income, rental share taken net, profit on debt grossed up with Zakat deducted from the profit itself — and compute taxable income for rate purposes for Marjan.
difficulty_basis: Member-level computations with gross-up, Zakat placement and rate-purpose income; several interacting rules.

summary: Full business computation for a restaurant chain: no sales adjustment for small cash invoices, 10% disallowance on NTN-less purchases, trademark amortization, withholding-default disallowance, lease interest, sublease rent under other sources, capital gain on listed shares at the correct rate, then set brought-forward losses and tax depreciation in the right order — lapsed 2019 loss, 50%-of-income cap on unabsorbed depreciation — before computing tax.
difficulty_basis: Seventeen-mark integrated computation across four heads with loss-ordering rules and rate traps; the longest question in the paper.

summary: Monthly sales-tax computation for a manufacturer-importer: third-schedule goods at retail price, inadmissible input on office equipment, imports at 130% of assessed value, reversal for the 180-day unpaid balance, unclaimed prior input, zero-rating for in-flight supplies, EPZ supply treatment, advances as taxable, discount mechanics, gift vouchers outside output tax, and further-tax applicability — without apportioning where none is needed.
difficulty_basis: Seventeen-mark sales-tax computation with a dozen distinct adjustments; tabular data needs careful reading.

summary: Where an author elects the beneficial treatment for a lump-sum royalty on a novel written over 30 months, decide how the receipt is spread across tax years for charging tax.
difficulty_basis: Beneficial-treatment rule for literary royalties; requires spreading logic, not simple receipt basis.

summary: Decide what enters taxable income when a resident sells her private car at a gain and her personal jewellery at a loss in the same year.
difficulty_basis: Personal-asset exclusion from capital assets; one-step application.

summary: Compute the correct value of supply for cement bought wholesale but sold at retail under the Third Schedule, with federal excise duty and sales tax layered on the retail price.
difficulty_basis: Third-schedule valuation mechanics with FED layered in; arithmetic trap.

summary: State how long a temporary sales-tax registration remains valid.
difficulty_basis: Pure recall of the temporary registration validity period.

summary: Identify which case cannot use the agreed assessment mechanism: Commissioner refusing a settlement offer, small tax liability, listed-company taxpayer, or a question-of-law dispute.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the agreed-assessment exclusions; listed-company and question-of-law distractors.

summary: Judge four claims about AOP taxation — separate entity, rate parity with non-salaried individuals, exempt member share where the AOP paid tax, and deductibility of a member's share of AOP loss.
difficulty_basis: Four statements on AOP taxation to sort; the loss-share statement is the trap.

summary: Decide which of four persons must file a wealth statement with the return: a salaried resident with tax already deducted, a non-resident filing a nil return for filer status, a dividend-only resident, and a first-time filer with modest income.
difficulty_basis: Four filer scenarios against the wealth-statement triggers; nil-return and dividend-only cases test the edges.

summary: Compute the taxable property income for leased open land: higher of actual rent and letting value, plus the non-adjustable deposit, less allowable property tax and capped collection charges.
difficulty_basis: Property-income computation with non-adjustable deposit, letting-value rule and collection-charge cap.

summary: In the most tax-efficient way, compute taxable income and tax or refund for an employee made redundant: salary for the months worked, rent-free flat, company car's personal-use benefit, interest-free loan benefit and partial waiver, purchase of the car at book value and resale, compensation under the scheme, unapproved gratuity, rental income from the financed flat, and spreading of the terminal benefits against prior years' average rates.
difficulty_basis: Ten-mark redundancy computation; the 'most tax efficient' instruction adds strategy to the adjustments.

summary: Judge whether five candidates — a High Court advocate, a CA in practice-employment, a cost accountant in own practice, an Inland Revenue officer in BS-20, and a BS-21 officer — qualify for appointment as members of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue, giving reasons.
difficulty_basis: Eligibility check across five profiles; each needs the right rule and a stated reason.

summary: Where an agency impounds undisclosed assets but source and value details are incomplete and no assessment exists, discuss whether the Commissioner can pass an order now, what kind of order it is, and how it is dealt with afterwards.
difficulty_basis: Unexplained-asset procedure; must name the right order and what follows it.

summary: Advise a sole proprietor on the tax treatment of flagged items — cash salary to a foreman, a cash electricity bill, rent paid from a personal account, and R&D for a process available but not yet used — quantifying each allowable deduction or add-back.
difficulty_basis: Advise-and-quantify format; cash-payment and mode-of-payment rules drive the add-backs.

summary: State three adverse consequences — ignoring surcharge and penalties — when a retailer installs POS machines but fails to integrate them with the FBR system, under the Income Tax Ordinance and the Sales Tax Act.
difficulty_basis: List three consequences across two statutes; needs specifics, not generalities.

summary: List the taxes the Federal Government is empowered to levy under the authority of Parliament.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the constitutional tax powers of Parliament; tested at T1.

summary: Under the ICAP Code of Ethics, explain the safeguards for reducing threats to an acceptable level when an audit firm prepares tax calculations involving accounting entries for a non-public-interest audit client.
difficulty_basis: Ethics application to a specific non-audit service for a non-PIE audit client.

summary: State the exceptions to the general rule that exports of goods are zero-rated under the Sales Tax Act.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the carve-outs from export zero-rating.

summary: Discuss how the Spanish rental income of Maria — a Spanish national employed in Karachi with no other Pakistan business — is taxed, where part of the rent lands in her Pakistani bank account.
difficulty_basis: Foreign-source rules for two individuals with different presence patterns; treaty ignored by instruction.

summary: Discuss how Zahid's Canadian salary — taxed at source in Canada, half remitted to Pakistan — is treated after his mid-year return to Pakistan.
difficulty_basis: Residential-status arithmetic plus foreign-salary and remittance treatment.

summary: Compute taxable income by head and tax payable with the return for a former employee: profit on debt grossed up from the 15% withholding, and capital gain on employee-share-scheme shares using the correct cost base and holding-period rate.
difficulty_basis: Two-head computation with share-scheme cost rules and withholding gross-up.

summary: Full computation for a sole-proprietor manufacturer: advance sales excluded, penalty and personal-loan interest disallowed, second-hand research equipment and imported plant depreciated correctly with installation costs, dividend grossed up with Zakat off the dividend, sublet rental with the old deposit refunded, capital gain on shares of a government-majority company, and unabsorbed depreciation capped at half of business income.
difficulty_basis: Eighteen-mark integrated computation; rental sublease, government-held shares and research-expense rules add variety.

summary: Monthly sales-tax computation for a manufacturer-exporter: apportion input across taxable, zero-rated and exempt streams, disallow input paid from a non-business account and on exempt-use raw material, admit cottage-industry purchases correctly, time the supply on payment patterns, handle the exempt-contract advance after the exemption's withdrawal, sales returns with notes, and the prior-month debit-note correction.
difficulty_basis: Eighteen-mark sales-tax computation; apportionment, cottage industry and contract-timing issues dominate.

summary: Pick the situation that best shows taxation used for a non-revenue objective in Pakistan — for example, raising duties on luxury imports to protect local industry rather than to fund spending.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the non-revenue roles of taxation; the luxury-import option is the clear signal.

summary: From a list of five properties — self-occupied house, rented house, agricultural land, office building and vacant commercial plot — compute the tax on deemed income, excluding the properties the law leaves out.
difficulty_basis: Deemed-income working across five properties with exclusions; arithmetic with traps.

summary: A company shifts from the normal year to a special year ending 30 September: map three accounting periods — a full normal year, a three-month transitional period, and the first full special year — to their tax years.
difficulty_basis: Special-tax-year mapping; three periods to three tax years.

summary: A practitioner advises on a cross-border deal without treaty expertise and the client suffers double tax: name the ethical principle most clearly breached.
difficulty_basis: Ethics principle identification from a competence failure.

summary: Compute taxable income under other sources for rental from a newly built industrial property (building plus plant and machinery) alongside dividend from an unlisted company.
difficulty_basis: Two-part computation: rental loss on a new industrial property plus dividend; the depreciation rates drive the answer.

summary: Choose which body — federal government, provincial government, local government or non-profit organisation — is a 'person' but not a 'company' under the Ordinance.
difficulty_basis: Definition recall distinguishing 'person' from 'company'.

summary: For a company with three branches in different cities, pick the correct sales-tax registration position: separate branch registrations, head-office-only registration, or optional registration.
difficulty_basis: Single rule on branch registration under the Sales Tax Act.

summary: Judge which statements are correct on destroying buyer-returned goods unfit for consumption: prior permission, supervision rank, and whether the input credit survives.
difficulty_basis: Three statements on destruction procedure; permission, supervision and input-credit points.

summary: For an AOP with two unequal partners: (i) compute the AOP's total and taxable income — adjusting for purchases without withholding, member salary, concessional rent from a member, commission to a member, and dividend from an exempt-income company; (ii) compute each member's total income, taxable income and tax, adding the AOP share for rate purposes, the listed-share capital gain net of brokerage, and the painting gain.
difficulty_basis: Twelve-mark two-part AOP question with member-level knock-ons; withholding and dividend gross-up are the traps.

summary: Compute total and taxable salary income for a new joiner: basic and medical allowance, medical reimbursement vs exemption, accommodation where the employer rents the employee's own property, capital gain on ex-employer shares from an old share scheme, and a receipt from an unapproved gratuity scheme.
difficulty_basis: Salary plus share-scheme and gratuity; the self-rented accommodation point is unusual.

summary: A Pakistani citizen returns after seven years in the UAE and receives UAE consultancy income into a Pakistani bank: discuss how the foreign-source income is taxed, including whether the returning-expatriate shield still applies.
difficulty_basis: Returning-expatriate exemption timing; needs the residence-year analysis first.

summary: The auditor of a public interest entity is asked to prepare current and deferred tax calculations for management: discuss under the Code of Ethics whether the firm may accept, weighing the self-review threat and available safeguards.
difficulty_basis: Ethics application: tax calculations for a public-interest audit client.

summary: Compute total and taxable income from a mixed basket — inherited jewellery, jewellery gain, profit on debt, share losses, government-securities gain, foreign business loss and other-sources loss — deciding what is income at all and what is chargeable.
difficulty_basis: Short computation; the exclusions (gift, exempt items) matter more than the arithmetic.

summary: Explain the loss treatment behind the computation: which losses set off against which income, what carries forward and for how long, and what lapses — covering speculation, foreign business and other-sources losses.
difficulty_basis: Loss set-off and carry-forward rules across heads and borders; the explanation carries the marks.

summary: Identify the individuals who must file a return of income purely because of assets owned, even where income is below the taxable threshold.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the asset-based filing triggers for individuals.

summary: A taxpayer files an offer of settlement before the Assessment Oversight Committee and the Committee proposes to modify it: explain his position if he agrees with the modification and if he disagrees.
difficulty_basis: Two scenarios on the settlement-offer outcome; the agree/disagree fork drives different consequences.

summary: Discuss whether a registered seller may claim input tax on a Rs 16 million supply where the buyer is unregistered, unregistered and dealing in exempt goods, registered but selling only third-schedule items, registered as an exporter, or a retailer.
difficulty_basis: Five buyer profiles; the Rs 10 million threshold and Tier-1 retailer distinction are the traps.

summary: A registered person ignores a Commissioner's notice and never files the sales-tax return: discuss what action the Commissioner may take and what recourse the taxpayer has against it.
difficulty_basis: Best-judgment assessment procedure plus the taxpayer's remedies; two-sided answer needed.

summary: Full head-wise computation for a food-ingredients sole proprietorship: strip sales tax out of sales, treat the destroyed imported machinery as a non-depreciable disposal with the insurance receipt, add back the bearer-cheque commission and personal costs, split the bank-loan interest between leasing and private use, compute property income on the leased plot with its deposit, and adjust brought-forward minimum tax.
difficulty_basis: Nineteen-mark computation with sales-tax-inclusive turnover and insurance mechanics; dense adjustments.

summary: Rebuild a manufacturer's sales-tax computation for the month: reject input on CREST-flagged and suspended suppliers and on head-office building material, time input on goods made available but collected later, correct the associate's discounted supply value, tax the surrendered insurance claim and the bank-auctioned pledged goods, charge further tax on the unregistered-retailer supply, and carry forward the excess input.
difficulty_basis: Sixteen-mark revision of a prepared computation; every line needs a verdict against the rules.

summary: Compute the chemical manufacturer's total income, taxable income and tax: adjust the slow-moving stock provision, disallow partners' salaries, treat partners' capital interest, handle the recovered bad debt against the earlier allowed amount, classify the pre-settlement derivative loss as speculation, and treat furniture moved to a partner's home as a disposal.
difficulty_basis: Eight-mark AOP computation; bad-debt recovery, derivative loss and furniture disposal are the discriminators.

summary: Compute the partner's total income, taxable income and tax: bring in her AOP share for rate purposes, tax the let-out plot on the higher of actual and market rent with the non-adjustable deposit, compute the capital gain on gifted foreign shares using the donor's market value as cost with foreign tax credit, and spread the book royalty.
difficulty_basis: Nine-mark partner computation spanning property, foreign shares and royalty; multi-head integration.

summary: State the other option available to the author for taxing her lump-sum royalty, without redoing the computation.
difficulty_basis: Short theory point on the royalty-spreading election.

summary: Compute the retiree's taxable income: final month's salary and allowances, leave encashment, recognised provident-fund principal and interest, approved gratuity, the waived slice of the interest-free loan, the laptop bought below market value, and the farewell gift.
difficulty_basis: Retirement-benefit computation with waivers and perquisites; each benefit has its own rule.

summary: Explain how the provident-fund and gratuity receipts would be treated if the funds were unrecognised and unapproved respectively, including which contributions stay taxable and the gratuity exemption limit.
difficulty_basis: Contrast exercise: recognised vs unrecognised funds; the exemption caps differ.

summary: Determine residential status for two visitors: a first-time arriver staying about six months, and a manufacturer present six months under a special calendar tax year.
difficulty_basis: Two presence-pattern cases; the special-tax-year twist decides the second.

summary: A taxpayer files an offer of settlement before the Assessment Oversight Committee and the Committee proposes changes: explain his position if he accepts the modification and if he rejects it.
difficulty_basis: Same settlement-offer fork as the 2026 model paper; agree vs disagree consequences.

summary: Compute the chargeable capital gains and tax on four disposals — a bungalow (ignoring FBR valuations), a gifted coin collection, antique furniture taken at fair market value — and explain why the residence-to-office table produces no gain or loss.
difficulty_basis: Eight-mark capital-gains set: FBR values, gifts, antiques at FMV, and the personal-use table exclusion.

summary: List the documents a taxpayer must maintain in relation to capital gains.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the record-keeping list for capital gains.

summary: A 16-year-old inherits a car and earns shop income: discuss how his income is charged — clubbed with the higher-income parent's — and whether he must file a return.
difficulty_basis: Minor's income clubbing plus the filing question; two linked conclusions.

summary: For a trader with branches in Kuwait (profit, tax paid abroad) and Syria (loss), discuss the Pakistan tax implications: carry-forward of the foreign loss and the foreign tax credit limited to the lower of foreign and Pakistan tax.
difficulty_basis: Foreign branch profits and losses with a foreign tax credit cap.

summary: Compute total income from a portfolio of properties — residence, son's apartment, business office, unbuilt plots, an unlet shop and a Dubai bungalow — taxing deemed income where due and giving reasons for each exclusion.
difficulty_basis: Eight-mark deemed-income sweep across seven properties; exclusions need reasons.

summary: Say whether each of five activities is taxable under the Sales Tax Act — salary, paid consultancy for a sibling's start-up, playing piano at a family party, maths tuition, and a hobby baker's festival stall — with reasons.
difficulty_basis: Five mini-scenarios testing the boundary of taxable activity.

summary: Where a supplier fails to deposit sales tax for financial reasons, explain the chargeability: the buyer and supplier are jointly and severally liable once knowledge or reasonable suspicion is established.
difficulty_basis: Joint-liability rule for unpaid supplier tax; short and pointed.

summary: For Rs 12 million of third-schedule goods supplied to an unregistered person, explain the chargeability — value at retail price — and the input-tax restriction beyond the Rs 10 million threshold.
difficulty_basis: Third-schedule supply to an unregistered person with the Rs 10 million input-tax threshold.

summary: List any four bases on which the Commissioner may suspend a registration without prior notice where fake invoices, evasion or fraud are suspected.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the four suspension triggers under the Sales Tax Rules.

summary: For three registered persons, compute sales tax payable or refundable and any carry-forward: net discounts correctly, third-schedule retail uplift, machines used wholly for exempt or taxable supplies (no apportionment), cottage-industry supplies with further tax, unregistered-purchase input, and the lower-of-input-or-90%-of-output rule.
difficulty_basis: Sixteen-mark three-person computation; apportionment and the 90%-of-output cap are the traps.

summary: The auditor of a public interest entity is asked to prepare its current and deferred tax calculations: discuss whether the firm may do so, distinguishing material from immaterial calculations and the safeguards for the self-review threat.
difficulty_basis: Ethics scenario for a public-interest audit client; materiality fork matters.

summary: Identify four ways taxes can serve a country's development beyond collecting revenue — such as steering investment, redistribution, and economic stabilisation.
difficulty_basis: Four development roles of tax beyond revenue; needs explanation, not just listing.

summary: Compute taxable salary for a manager who joined mid-year: 11 months' salary with the medical-allowance exemption on basic, the company car's personal-use benefit net of the salary deduction, gain on disposing of employee share rights taxed as salary, pension from the former employer, and Zakat as a tax credit.
difficulty_basis: Salary computation with share-rights disposal and pension; the 11-month trap is the classic error.

summary: From a year of postings across the UK, UAE and Pakistan, assess an individual's residential status using every prescribed criterion rather than day-counting alone.
difficulty_basis: Presence-pattern case needing all residence criteria, not just the 183-day count.

summary: Prepare the wealth statement and the wealth reconciliation statement for the year: revalue the listed shares at cost, record the trade-in car with the unpaid price differential as a liability, account for the loan repayment, gifts and personal spending.
difficulty_basis: Full wealth statement plus reconciliation; asset valuation and liability recognition are the traps.

summary: Compute the chargeable amounts and tax on five disposals — a packaging machine used for FTR exports, an exported cutting machine, fire-destroyed antique vases settled by insurance, a gifted parrot, and unlisted shares — stating the head of income and why any gain or loss is ignored, with separate-block tax where it applies.
difficulty_basis: Eleven-mark disposal set with FTR vs normal-regime splits; the export-machine and vase points are subtle.

summary: Discuss why the packaging machine — used exclusively for income taxed under the final tax regime — is treated the way it is on disposal, with no depreciation in its written-down value.
difficulty_basis: Short justification of the FTR-machine treatment.

summary: Compute taxable income by head for an individual with Kenyan salary and rental income — exempting the salary, taxing rent at the higher of actual and market value with capped collection charges and allowable taxes and interest — plus property income from a newly leased factory with its renovation cost depreciated.
difficulty_basis: Ten-mark head-wise computation with foreign rental and a pre-let factory; many moving parts.

summary: Without redoing numbers, explain how the answer changes if the Kenya job had started a year earlier — testing whether the foreign-salary exemption still holds for the current year.
difficulty_basis: Conceptual: does an earlier foreign posting change the current-year answer?

summary: Full computation for a power-tools manufacturer: exclude the advance, write stock to net realisable value correctly, disallow the advance-tax penalty and the personal loan interest, amortise the software over days used, claim the disability ramps, then set brought-forward losses and tax depreciation in order — speculation loss only against speculation income, listed-securities loss within its window, and the bearer-cheque loan under other sources.
difficulty_basis: Nineteen-mark sole-proprietorship computation; loss-ordering and speculation set-off are the discriminators.

summary: Monthly sales-tax computation for a personal-care manufacturer: third-schedule goods at retail price, imports at retail price with the higher rate, hire-purchase machine at the correct value, cash-paid input disallowed, 180-day reversal on unpaid shaving kits, zero-rating for in-flight supplies but not for EPZ staff consumption, debt-settlement supply at its value, partial deliveries, further-tax limits, and correct apportionment.
difficulty_basis: Twenty-mark sales-tax computation with hire-purchase, EPZ and in-flight supplies; very dense.

summary: A newly registered manufacturer never starts trading and files no returns: discuss the duty to file nil returns and the consequences of not filing.
difficulty_basis: Nil-return duty for an inactive registrant; short recall.

summary: Discuss the Commissioner's powers where a registered person files no returns and has no taxable activity — including deregistration — rather than merely issuing a notice.
difficulty_basis: Commissioner's powers over an inactive registrant; deregistration point.

summary: For five independent cases — goods returned by registered and unregistered buyers in different months, and under- or over-stated supply values later corrected — state which debit or credit note each party issues and the effect on each party's sales-tax liability, in the required table format.
difficulty_basis: Five return-of-goods and error-correction cases in a fixed table format; document and liability effect each time.

summary: List the factors a firm weighs when evaluating the level of threats created by providing any tax service to an audit client.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the threat-evaluation factors for tax services to audit clients.

summary: Briefly explain the indirect taxes applicable in Pakistan, describing each rather than merely naming them.
difficulty_basis: Describe — not just name — the indirect taxes operating in Pakistan.

summary: Full head-wise computation for a food-ingredients sole proprietorship: deduct sales tax from turnover, do not re-apply the stated trade discount, treat the fire-destroyed imported machine as a disposal rather than a depreciable asset, add back the claim-lodging cost, capitalise the mixer at the right cost without customs duty in its base, disallow bearer-cheque and personal outlays, split the bank-loan interest between the leased plot and private use, compute property income net of expenses, and adjust minimum tax and its brought-forward credit.
difficulty_basis: Eighteen-mark computation; the insurance-destroyed machinery and loan-interest split are the discriminators.

summary: For an AOP with two unequal partners: (i) compute the AOP's total and taxable income — 20% disallowance on purchases without withholding, member salary, rent to a member at the concessional amount, commission to a member, and the FTR dividend grossed up; (ii) compute each member's total income, taxable income and tax, with the AOP share for rate purposes, the listed-share gain net of brokerage at the right rate, and the painting gain.
difficulty_basis: Eleven-mark two-part AOP question; FTR dividend gross-up is the key step.

summary: Compute total and taxable salary income: basic and medical allowance with the reimbursement correctly classified, accommodation where the employer rents the employee's own property taxed on the right value, the ex-employer share-scheme gain on the correct cost, and the unapproved gratuity receipt within its exemption limit.
difficulty_basis: Salary with self-rented accommodation and share-scheme gain; several exemption traps.

summary: For three foreign entities — a branch office, a liaison office limited to negotiating orders, and short-stay consultancy staff — decide whether each has a permanent establishment in Pakistan, with reasons.
difficulty_basis: Concept not examinable under the 2025 scheme; excluded per Bilal's standing direction.
exclusion_reason: Tests permanent establishment of foreign entities — not covered in the 2025-scheme CAF-2 syllabus (no mention in the Sep-26 study text); excluded per the direction to carry forward only topics still in the current scheme.

summary: Decide whether three companies are public or private for tax purposes: a delisted company, an unlisted company 49% held by a foreign-government-owned company, and a company with 30% federal, 20% provincial and 50% private holding — applying the listing-date and 50% government-ownership tests.
difficulty_basis: Three company profiles against the public-company definition; government-holding thresholds decide.

summary: Compute total and taxable income from the mixed basket — ignoring the inherited jewellery as a receipt, taxing the jewellery gain and profit on debt, and handling the share losses, government-securities gain, foreign business loss and other-sources loss — without classifying by head.
difficulty_basis: Short computation; the gift and the exempt items must be left out.

summary: Explain the loss treatment: set-off of private- and public-company share losses against each other, other-sources loss against the jewellery gain with no carry-forward, and the foreign business loss position.
difficulty_basis: Loss set-off and carry-forward map across five loss types; the explanation is the substance.

summary: Identify the individuals who must file a return of income because of assets owned, even where income is below the taxable threshold.
difficulty_basis: Recall of the asset-based filing triggers.

summary: A Pakistani citizen returns after seven years abroad and receives UAE consultancy income into a Pakistani bank: discuss the tax implications, including the returning-expatriate exemption across the relevant years.
difficulty_basis: Returning-expatriate timing; the exemption window is the point.

summary: Discuss how the Pakistan-paid salary of a British official assisting geophysicists is taxed, giving the correct rationale and the conditions for any exemption.
difficulty_basis: Exemption conditions for an international-organisation employee; rationale matters, not just the answer.

summary: For an office building, an ex-army allotted plot, and cultivated agricultural land with farmhouse, discuss the deemed-income treatment first assuming the owner is on the Active Taxpayers' List and then assuming he is not.
difficulty_basis: Deemed-income analysis under two ATL scenarios; calculation not required, reasoning is.

summary: Rebuild the manufacturer's monthly sales-tax computation: deny input on CREST-flagged and suspended-registration purchases and on head-office building material, admit input on goods made available in the month, value the associate's discounted supply correctly, tax the surrendered insurance claim and the bank-auctioned goods, keep further tax separate from output tax on unregistered-retailer supplies, and apportion input between taxable and zero-rated streams.
difficulty_basis: Fifteen-mark revision of a prepared computation; CREST, suspension and further-tax points.

summary: Discuss whether a registered seller may claim input tax on a Rs 16 million supply where the buyer is unregistered, unregistered and dealing in exempt goods, registered but selling only third-schedule items, registered as an exporter, or a retailer — distinguishing Tier-1 from other retailers.
difficulty_basis: Five buyer profiles with the threshold and Tier-1 distinctions.

summary: A registered person ignores the Commissioner's notice and never files: discuss the best-judgment assessment the Commissioner may make and the course open to the taxpayer against it.
difficulty_basis: Best-judgment assessment and taxpayer remedies; the expected focus, not suspension or SIM blocking.

summary: Briefly discuss the broad principles governing the levy of taxes — going beyond naming them to explain each.
difficulty_basis: Principles need discussion, not mere listing.

summary: Briefly explain the pillars of tax administration that protect taxpayers and check misuse of authority by tax officials, describing each pillar.
difficulty_basis: Pillars need description; naming alone earns little.

summary: Revise a footwear AOP's computation: correct the withholding-default disallowance, add back the office-space down payment and the multi-year software licence, move interest on term deposits to other sources gross, tax the ministerial award, disallow the supplier-advance bad debt, classify the waived rent correctly, cap the new car's cost at Rs 7.5 million with no initial allowance, and compute the tax loss on the old car's sale with apportioned consideration.
difficulty_basis: Sixteen-mark AOP revision; capital-expenditure add-backs and the motor-vehicle cost cap dominate.

summary: Compute taxable property income across a house, a flat and an open plot: pro-rate rents to the correct periods, handle non-adjustable deposits on receipt and refund, tax the flat at fair rental value, allow repair allowance only on constructed property, cap collection charges at the lower of actual and 4%, and treat the generator's rent and disposal under other sources and capital gains on its actual cost.
difficulty_basis: Eleven-mark property computation with FMV-vs-actual and deposit rules; the generator disposal adds a capital-gain layer.

summary: Define speculation business with its specified exclusions, and explain how its taxation differs from non-speculation business — especially that non-speculation losses can shelter certain other heads while speculation losses cannot.
difficulty_basis: Definition plus the exclusions and the set-off asymmetry; examinees knew the definition but missed the rest.

summary: For a chronic non-filer off the Active Taxpayers' List, discuss the FBR's administrative enforcement powers to compel filing — including the Income Tax General Order — and the preconditions before they can be used.
difficulty_basis: Enforcement powers and preconditions; the ITGO point is the discriminator.

summary: Outline what a persistent non-filer faces if non-compliance continues, ignoring penalties and prosecution under the general sections.
difficulty_basis: Consequences of continued non-compliance, excluding general penalties by instruction.

summary: Explain the taxability of a foreign consultant's Pakistan-stay income paid from London with no withholding, grounding the conclusion in her residential status.
difficulty_basis: Residential-status-driven taxability; the short-term-resident distractor must be rejected.

summary: Discuss the circumstances in which the consultant's income could qualify for exemption, referring to the correct exemption requirements.
difficulty_basis: Exemption conditions for international-organisation staff; the relevant requirements, not the short-term-resident rules.

summary: For a retailer, an exempt-supplies dealer, a manufacturer, an exporter and a dividend-only widow, discuss whether each must file an income-tax return on income grounds alone, with the applicable threshold.
difficulty_basis: Five profiles against the income-based filing test; threshold reasoning needed.

summary: For the same five persons, discuss whether each must file a sales-tax return, identifying the correct category such as Tier-1 retailer where relevant.
difficulty_basis: Same five profiles against sales-tax return duties; Tier-1 status matters.

summary: State whether each case is a dividend with reasons: assets distributed on liquidation, a foreign branch remitting after-tax profits, and a finance company lending to a shareholder on commercial terms.
difficulty_basis: Three dividend-definition cases; each turns on a different limb of the definition.

summary: Mark five loss statements true or false with reasons: foreign vs Pakistan source set-off, other-sources loss carry-forward, private vs public share losses, the six-year capital-loss window, and whether members can use an AOP's loss.
difficulty_basis: Five TRUE/FALSE statements on loss set-off; each false one needs its correction.

summary: Compute a CEO's taxable salary and tax: monthly salary, annual bonus set against the loan, school-fee reimbursement kept out of the section 60D allowance, the interest-free loan's waiver and benchmark-rate benefit, surcharge above Rs 10 million, and the employer-borne tax grossed up by the reciprocal method.
difficulty_basis: Salary with loan waiver, school fees and employer-borne tax; gross-up and surcharge traps.

summary: Discuss the tax treatment for the recipient of an Rs 800,000 gift in three cases: in-kind from an uncle, cash from a father, and in-kind from a close friend — naming the head of income where it is taxable.
difficulty_basis: Gift rules by relationship and form; head-of-income point for the taxable case.

summary: Revise a manufacturer's monthly computation: apportion input across taxable, zero-rated and exempt supplies, tax third-schedule goods at retail price, reverse input on destroyed goods, treat the domestic flight supply as taxable, tax free samples and personal-use withdrawals, leave the warranty replacements untaxed, admit the old unpaid invoices, and apply further tax only where it belongs.
difficulty_basis: Seventeen-mark computation with apportionment and several trap adjustments.

summary: Discuss the temporary sales-tax registration rules: when it is granted, how long it stays valid, how it is issued, what restrictions apply, and what the holder must comply with.
difficulty_basis: Temporary registration: grant, validity, procedure and compliance in one answer.

summary: For five claims about tax systems — taxes only on income, payment by willingness, alignment with economic objectives, enactment by the executive, and imposition by international bodies — justify why each is incorrect.
difficulty_basis: Five incorrect statements; each needs its refutation tied to a system characteristic.

summary: List five ethical responsibilities of the tax-implementing authorities, stating each fully rather than as a bare heading.
difficulty_basis: Five ethical duties of the tax authorities; full statements expected.
